calls.reason: About 19 months on, the Fed paper finds coder employment still growing, though more slowly. Anthropic's report shows hiring cuts but continued human oversight and growing absolute technical hiring. Nothing shows broad replacement.

The Feb 2025 study of 127 real maintainability issues found most LLM fixes introduced errors or new maintainability problems. That fits the modest claim that tools did not magically solve maintenance.

The novice study shows little review of generated code, but not large hard-to-maintain codebases. Veracode's security failures are not tied to beginners' overdependence. Both consequences remain unshown.

In February 2025, SWE-Lancer found frontier models failed most real freelance engineering tasks, including bug fixes and proposal selection. Anthropic's capability claims are company statements that do not show human expertise was unnecessary.

The GovTech pilot and the 2024 interview study report developers finding AI helpful for new languages and libraries. Anthropic's later RCT found lower mastery overall, but comprehension-focused use did better, which fits a modest 'can help' claim.

The Stanford payroll data shows employment of developers aged 22-25 down nearly 20%, while older developers grew. That is mixed evidence, and there is no deadline for an indefinite claim about obsolescence.
